clue.text: Ordeal pleb suffers is worthy of contempt

indicators.note: the words ordeal pleb suffer a battering here, so their letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A commoner going through an ordeal is treated as beneath contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers' is the anagram signal on ORDEAL PLEB; 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deplorable deserves condemnation, the same as meriting scorn.

clue.text: Rude beauty scratching bottom makes bloomer

parts.note: blue jokes are rude or smutty ones

indicators.note: scratching out the bottom letter removes the last letter of the word for beauty

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A coarse beauty scratching her backside commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder or underwear, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebell is a flower, and a bloomer is a plant that flowers.

clue.text: Look in wonder at old boy that's upended outhouse

parts.note: to gaze at something is to look at it in wonder

indicators.note: upended in a down clue means the letters for old boy are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at a former pupil who has been tipped over in a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a garden summerhouse, a small building separate from the main house.

clue.text: Coach popular with supporter around club

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: around says the supporter word goes round the club letter

parts.note: a strut is a structural support
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A fashionable coach backed by a fan who hangs around the football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to teach or train them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Group using some bass or treble

indicators.note: using some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement drawing on some low or high voices.
explanation.definitionFit: To assort is to sort into groups or classify, so the verb group fits.

clue.text: Paper Arab leader put round European cheese

indicators.note: put round says the newspaper letters enclose the European letter

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper wraps up an Arab chief's European cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Sick of Paris, having eaten English lunch?

indicators.note: having eaten says the French word swallows the English letter

parts.note: mal is French for ill or bad, the language of Paris

explanation.surface: Fed up with Paris, someone stuffed with English food at lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick of Paris' reads as weary of the city; it means the French word for sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is one example of a sitting for food, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A clergyman cuddling daughter is direct

indicators.note: cuddling says the clergyman word wraps around the daughter letter

parts.note: a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A vicar hugging his daughter is plainly straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direct' looks like an adjective meaning straightforward; it is the verb meaning manage.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer an organisation is to run or manage it, a verb sense of direct.

clue.text: Madman eagerly crashed into old Escort

indicators.note: the words madman eagerly have crashed and broken up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lunatic eagerly smashed into a vintage Ford Escort car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escort' looks like the Ford car model; it means a companion, here traditionally a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical follower of Jesus was long portrayed in tradition as a reformed prostitute, an escort of ancient times.

clue.text: Rip off an item of clothing

definitions.meaning: a warm zip-up jacket of synthetic wool

explanation.surface: Someone tears off a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to cheat someone of money; the noun is a soft warm jacket.

clue.text: Hand out endless beer? That's logical!

parts.note: to ration supplies is to hand them out in portions

indicators.note: endless means the beer word loses its final letter

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Serving unlimited beer would be the sensible thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational thinking follows reason, so it is sound and logical.

clue.text: Type of jazz released due to head of Mercury

parts.note: free means released
for can mean because of, as in famous for

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A style of jazz record put out by the Mercury label's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Free-form jazz is improvised without fixed structure, a recognised genre.

clue.text: Posh performer taking bit of penicillin will make recovery

indicators.note: taking says the posh and performer pieces take in the bit of penicillin

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for upper-class, posh
a turn is a variety act or performer

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A smart entertainer on antibiotics will get better.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is an improvement, as in an economic recovery.

clue.text: Large dress needs alterations whatever the cost

indicators.note: a dress needing alterations gets refashioned, so the letters of large dress are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big frock must be altered, no matter the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Regardless means no matter what, despite any consequences.

clue.text: A shocking bit of weather seen by the globe?

definitions.text: A shocking bit of weather seen by the globe?

parts.words: A shocking bit of weather seen by the globe?
parts.note: an electrical weather phenomenon that appears as a glowing sphere, so it is seen as a globe; the surface suggests a world-wide event

explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking' is literal, electric, and 'by the globe' suggests worldwide but means in the shape of a sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare phenomenon is a luminous floating orb seen during thunderstorms.

clue.text: Liberal bringing in money for education

parts.note: earning is bringing in money

explanation.surface: A Liberal promises more funding for schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is the acquisition of knowledge, the same thing as education.

clue.text: Ultimately, need hint to get a letter jumble

indicators.note: a letter jumble is a mix-up of characters, so the letters of need hint are rearranged

explanation.surface: In the end, a word puzzle needs a hint to crack it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually or finally, the same as ultimately.

clue.text: American ace on medicine is petrifying female

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the American ace comes after medicine

parts.note: US means American
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A US flying ace on drugs is a frightening woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gorgon of Greek myth whose gaze turned onlookers to stone.

clue.text: Naked relation briefly appears on commercial

indicators.note: appears on in a down clue means the shortened relation sits above the commercial
briefly means the relation word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an uncle is a relation
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A relative turns up nude in a TV advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclad means without clothes, a synonym of naked.

clue.text: People providing help for a few punters

parts.note: punters are betters, people who place bets; the a before them makes a few of them

explanation.surface: Assistants are on hand for a small band of gamblers.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A BETTERS: a handful of punters.
explanation.definitionFit: Abetters are those who aid or encourage someone, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: One who is taking seven around small festival

indicators.note: around says the diner word goes round the small letter

parts.note: seven is a cross-reference to the entry at 7 across, a lunch; someone taking that lunch is a diner, one who consumes food

explanation.surface: Someone carting seven people round a little fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seven' is not a number but the clue at 7 across, so the solver needs that light first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast of the Resurrection is a major spring holiday.

clue.text: Getting drunk? I can't with ale or port

indicators.note: getting drunk scrambles things, so the letters of i can't and ale are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to get drunk on ale or port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a Mediterranean harbour city in south-east Spain.

clue.text: Fat boy eats last grain of sugar

indicators.note: eats says the boy word swallows the other letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the last grain of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A boy getting fat eats the last of the sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is pig fat used in cooking.

clue.text: Short periods of time can be magical things

definitions.meaning: brief stretches, as in a cold snap or a stint
incantations or charms cast by a witch

explanation.surface: Brief moments can feel like enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both brief stints and witches' incantations.

clue.text: After dressing, greet a nice relative

indicators.note: dressing means arranging or reworking, so the letters of greet a nice are rearranged

explanation.surface: Once dressed, someone welcomes a pleasant family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's granddaughter is a kinswoman two generations down.

clue.text: Loud sound out of one hooter

indicators.note: out of says the one letter is taken out of the sound word

parts.note: a noise is a loud sound
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A loud blast comes from a single car horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' looks like a horn; it is slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooter is British slang for the organ of smell on the face.
